_readme: Copy this file to user_config.json and edit it with YOUR values. user_config.json is gitignored, so your personal data (account balances, strategy picks) never reaches the repository. Every key is optional: anything missing falls back to the documented defaults in main.py's USER DASHBOARD. Strategy names must match the keys shown by `python main.py --list`.
_window_note: There is no START_DATE / END_DATE any more, and adding them back does nothing but print a warning. A window you choose is a result you chose. The engine runs a fixed era (from 2004-11, the first month a strategy rather than a passive benchmark can be measured) to the last COMPLETE month in the data, and reports every strategy across pre-registered market regimes dated by the NBER, the FOMC, the BLS and the S&P 500. See common/eras.py.
_cost_note: COST_PCT_PER_SIDE is ONE-WAY, charged per leg on the notional actually traded, so 0.001 means a full A->B rotation costs 0.2%. This is Keller's stated assumption. It replaces TRANSACTION_COST_PCT, which still loads (with a deprecation notice) but charged half as much.
_execution_note: EXECUTION_CONVENTION: 'next_open' fills at the open of the session AFTER the signal, which is what after-hours GTC orders actually do. 'signal_close' fills at the signal's own close -- look-ahead by construction, kept only to reproduce pre-audit numbers. Never quote a signal_close result.
_coverage_note: COVERAGE_POLICY: 'trim' shortens the window when a strategy's assets did not exist yet, and says which ticker binds. 'strict' refuses to measure it at all.
_selection_note: The dashboard picker is a CHECKLIST, everything ticked by default, and it saves what you turned OFF rather than what you turned on. That is what EXCLUDED_STRATEGIES is: an empty list means run every registered strategy, so a variant added to the registry later shows up on its own. The old STRATEGIES allow-list still loads and still wins if present, but it froze the line-up to whatever the registry held the day it was written. Names must match `python main.py --list`.
_controls_note: SHOW_CONTROLS reveals the two degenerate single-asset diagnostics (HAA_G1_Simple, BAA_G1_SPY). They are not portfolios: they exist so a family's record can be split into its timing rule and its universe, and they are excluded from the selection statistics. HAA_G1_Simple is nonetheless paper-faithful (HAA S6, Fig 12) and regularly ranks top-three, which is the point of keeping it available.
_exploratory_note: SHOW_EXPLORATORY reveals the eight 3x leveraged variants (role=exploratory). They are real strategies with real signals, measured and ranked in full and flagged (expl) -- but excluded from the selection statistics and hidden by default, because NO 3x product predates 2008-11: not one of their drawdowns has been measured through a bear market, and LEVERAGE.md section 7 puts a 3x portfolio through 2008 near -95%. Each *_G3_Leveraged_3X twins a *_G3_Leveraged_2X on the same universe and the same signal, which is the only place in this repo where the leverage LEVEL is the single changed variable -- measured, four pairs out of four raise CAGR while lowering both Sortino and UPI. Separate from SHOW_CONTROLS on purpose: wanting a 2x-vs-3x comparison is not the same as wanting the single-asset diagnostics.
_rank_note: RANK_BY: 'cagr' | 'sharpe' | 'sortino' | 'upi' | 'vol' | 'max_dd'. Whichever you pick, the report prints the rank correlation of that ordering between disjoint sub-periods -- it comes out near zero. Rank to describe, not to select.
_ranked_window_note: RANKED_WINDOW_POLICY: 'strategies' (default) lets only published entries set the shared ranked window; the leverage-forced G4 wraps were costing every other row 19 months and hiding 2008 from the headline drawdown column. They are still measured, in a separate block. 'all' forces one window over everything.
_segment_note: SEGMENT_TOP_N: how many strategies to list under each regime segment in the per-regime leaderboards. Only strategies covering a segment IN FULL are ranked -- one that entered late shows the recovery without the fall.
_partition_note: REGIME_PARTITIONS: which of the four pre-registered partitions the dashboard DISPLAYS. Omit the key for all four. This is a display choice and nothing else -- each partition is independently exhaustive and disjoint, so hiding one changes nothing about the others. There is deliberately no way to hide SEGMENTS inside a partition: dropping some would stop it tiling the era, and "show me only the interesting periods" is exactly the window-picking this design exists to forbid. For stress episodes alone, read the named-crises table (common/regimes.py), which is non-exhaustive by construction and says so.
_cache_note: CACHE_REFRESH_HOURS: hours before the daily cache re-checks Yahoo. It used to re-download 90 days of every ticker on EVERY run (9.1s and a 10MB rewrite, to learn nothing). Signals come from complete months and live sizing quotes prices separately, so an intraday-stale daily cache cannot change a decision. Set 0, or pass --refresh, to force it.
_strict_gaps_note: STRICT_GAPS: refuse any ticker with an interior data gap longer than 5 trading days instead of forward-filling past it. Default true. Set false to proceed through a data outage; the report header then names every gap the run carried.
_sizing_note: The three inputs to the SUSTAINABLE MARGIN LEVERAGE section (and the dashboard's 'Max margin' column). SAFETY_FACTOR_K is the only preference the sizing module has, in MULTIPLES OF DRAWDOWN: 5 prudent / 3 balanced / 2 aggressive. It is also the whole grey zone -- at k=5 nothing in the registry supports margin at all, at k=3 the best entry is ~1.27x, at k=2 ~1.47x. MAINTENANCE_BASE is the assumed house requirement on an ordinary ETF position; a leveraged product is charged this times the fund's OWN multiple (2x -> 60%, 3x -> 90%), so a 3x book cannot be margined at all. FINRA Rule 4210(c) floors the base at 25%. BORROWING_CAPACITY_LEVERAGE is the only input that needs a real broker: leave it null and that cap is reported unbounded rather than guessed. If you ever fill it in, it must be the TAXABLE account's equity -- registered accounts do not permit margin, so a household total would describe a portfolio you cannot hold.
